title: Huangshan Is in Cloud 200 Days a Year — Here's the Day to Climb | China Travel Expert
description:
Huangshan is wrapped in mist about 200 days a year. Pick the wrong day and you'll pay ¥190 to stare at white.

Huangshan — the Yellow Mountains in Anhui — is the most-painted peak in China: granite spires, pines growing straight out of bare rock, and the famous "sea of clouds" that floods the valleys and leaves the summits floating. The problem is timing. The summit is shrouded in cloud roughly 200 days a year, and the full ticket is ¥190 in peak season (Mar–Nov), ¥95 off-peak (Dec–Feb), valid three days. The good news: the sea of clouds isn't random — it's most likely in winter and early spring, with better than 80% odds, and it shows up best the morning after light rain, when the valleys fill and the peaks rise above the cloud.

🧭 Expert Tip: go the morning right after light rain between November and March, and buy the 3-day ticket so one foggy day doesn't sink the trip — you can try again the next morning.

黄山一年约200天云雾缭绕——挑错日子，¥190看一片白；雨后清晨、冬春季节，云海概率超80%。
